audit.title: DataLink
audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual overview of Chainlink DataLink with a crisp, liftable opening definition and clean section boundaries. Its biggest GEO strength is answer-first extractability — most sections open with a self-contained claim an engine can quote. Its biggest opportunities are (1) concrete specifics: the page leans on vague quantifiers ("wide range," "fast," "robust") where numbers, update intervals, and supported-chain counts belong, and (2) machine-readability: no JSON-LD, canonical URL, or last-updated date was found in the served HTML. This is solid documentation held back from Strong by thin specificity and missing structured metadata.

recommendations.title: Add a Pull vs Push comparison table
recommendations.issue: Pull/Push differences are split across two prose bullet lists; 0 tables on page.
recommendations.change: Add a table with rows Infrastructure / Access methods / Latency / Use cases / On-chain cost model, columns Pull vs Push, each cell with the canonical fact (e.g. Pull → "Chainlink Data Streams, REST/WebSocket/Go/Rust SDK, sub-second, fetch-on-demand").
recommendations.why: Engines extract *reasons* and build justified "which should I use" answers from tables far more reliably than from parallel prose.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete numbers
recommendations.issue: "sub-second data resolution," "wide range of… data types" — only 4 numerals, 0 with units.
recommendations.change: State counts and intervals: number of data-type categories offered (the list has ~11 — say so), typical push update intervals, pull latency figures, number of supported chains. Quantify "tens of trillions" with the cited figure.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `about: "DataLink"`, `dateModified`, and a self-referencing canonical link; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust; verify whether these are client-injected before treating as fully absent.

recommendations.title: Add a decision/FAQ section with symptom- and intent-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: No FAQ; headings are concept-titled ("Pull Delivery"), not question-phrased.
recommendations.change: Add H3s like "When should I use pull vs push delivery?", "How do I access DataLink data via REST or WebSocket?", "What data types does DataLink support?" — each answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by intent and symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal pull-delivery fetch snippet
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; agents get only SDK links.
recommendations.change: Add a short, language-tagged REST/WebSocket example (or curl) showing a signed-report fetch and where verification happens, with a link to full SDK docs.
recommendations.why: Runnable, self-contained snippets are directly liftable by coding agents completing integration tasks.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source / spec citations
recommendations.issue: 0 links to primary sources; externals are marketing pages.
recommendations.change: Link "Decentralized Oracle Network (DON)" and "commit-and-reveal / frontrunning" to their canonical Chainlink concept/spec pages on first use.
recommendations.why: Inline links to canonical definitions raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers in place of figures: "wide range," "fast," "quickly," "robust," "some."
Mild marketing fluff: "launch new markets faster than ever before," "gaining a first-mover advantage."
Three unresolved "(Image: Image)" placeholders — no alt text; contributes nothing to extraction and should carry descriptive captions.
No stale-content risk visible, but absence of any date means freshness is unverifiable.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; confirm it lists this URL.
JSON-LD/canonical/date may be injected site-wide via the docs framework; pass raw `<head>` through the CLI to confirm before treating metadata as fully absent.
Third-party/earned citations (analyst coverage, partner blogs) are off-page and not scored here.
